claims.expected_type: ∀ m : Nat, (MathOS.satTerms m).length = 3 ^ m ∧ (MathOS.satTerms m).Nodup ∧ (∀ w ∈ MathOS.satTerms m, MathOS.satCoefficient w ≠ 0)
claims.research_claim: For every natural number m, the indexed three-choice SAT-factor word list has length 3^m, contains no duplicates, and has nonzero integer signs.
claims.scope: The inductive, syntactic list of independent factor-choice words defined by MathOS.satTerms and MathOS.satCoefficient; not a generic multivariate polynomial ring.
claims.limitations: Does not establish polynomial-ring support correspondence, lower bounds for arbitrary SAT algorithms, P versus NP, novelty, or any Millennium Prize solution.

claims.research_claim: For every finite number m of independently indexed factors, the explicitly generated MathOS three-choice words have exactly 3^m list entries.
claims.scope: The list length of the recursively constructed syntactic term words only; this is a finite combinatorial fact and not an algorithmic complexity lower bound.
claims.limitations: Does not prove terms are noncanceling in arbitrary polynomial representations, nor does it imply anything about the worst-case runtime of all SAT solvers.
